findings.title: Unguarded `organization_context.member` access raises AttributeError for API-key and org-token requests on every call, not only when `optimized_pagination=true`
findings.description: Line 71 (`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) runs unconditionally, before the `use_optimized` check on line 73. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346), and the service sets it to `None` whenever `user_id is None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/impl.py:123-140). API-key and org-token requests authenticate as `AnonymousUser()` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:518 and :552), so `request.user.id` is `None`. For such a request, `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`, and the expression evaluates `None.has_global_access`, which raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500. The permission check still passes when the token holds `org:write`, because `OrganizationAuditPermission.scope_map["GET"]` is `["org:write"]` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:110-111), so `get()` runs. Before this diff those requests returned 200 through `DateTimePaginator`. The fix is to read `member = organization_context.member` and test `member is not None and member.has_global_access`, and to evaluate it only when `use_optimized` is true.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to a `datetime`, so every non-empty optimized page raises TypeError
findings.description: The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:80), and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). `get_item_key` copies the numeric `Paginator` implementation: `value = getattr(item, self.key)` yields a `datetime`, and `math.ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key function on the first result when `cursor.value` is 0 (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122) and on the last result (line 137), so any response with at least one row crashes. The correct conversion is in `DateTimePaginator.get_item_key` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-236), which converts via `strftime` to milliseconds. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` should reuse that logic, for example by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` passes the raw millisecond integer into a datetime comparison
findings.description: `DateTimePaginator` encodes cursor values as millisecond integers (paginator.py:233-236) and decodes them with `datetime.fromtimestamp(float(cursor.value) / self.multiplier)` (paginator.py:238-241). The optimized version returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` then appends that integer as a SQL parameter for `<table>.datetime >= %s` or `<=` (paginator.py:112-126). Comparing a timestamp column with an integer is a type error on PostgreSQL, which Sentry uses, so any follow-up request carrying a cursor with `optimized_pagination=true` fails. The first-page crash in the previous finding currently hides this, but it is a separate defect and remains once that one is fixed.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed into a queryset slice on the advanced path and raise an exception
findings.description: On the `enable_advanced_features` branch, `start_offset = cursor.offset` is passed through without a sign check, and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is evaluated. `Cursor.from_string` accepts a signed offset because it calls `int(bits[1])` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59), and `get_cursor` forwards the value unchanged (src/sentry/utils/pagination_factory.py:46-51). Django 5.2.1 is pinned (requirements-frozen.txt:36), and `QuerySet` rejects negative slice bounds. A caller who is a superuser or has global access can send `optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-1:0` and get a 500. The comment on lines 874-876 says Django "handles negative slicing automatically", which is incorrect. This path therefore never returns rows and can only fail.

findings.title: `BasePaginator` now silently clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0 for every paginated endpoint instead of rejecting them
findings.description: The base paginator now computes `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. Before this change, a negative offset on any cursor reached the queryset slice and failed. Now a malformed next-cursor with a negative offset returns the first page as if the offset were 0, and no error is raised. The change affects all paginators that inherit `BasePaginator`, not only audit logs. Prev-cursors with negative offsets still reach the slice unchanged, so the handling is inconsistent between the two directions. The comment's justification ("the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is also false, because the queryset rejects negative bounds (see the finding above).
